title: Quote of the day by filmmaker James Cameron on AI: 'All of human art and human experience put into a blender'…
excerpt: Although AI is increasingly being incorporated into the production process, not everyone is on the same page
content_html:
The rise of generative AI has undoubtedly lowered the barrier to entry for creating film, with individuals as well as massive production companies leveraging the technology in different ways. But many, including Academy Award-winning filmmaker James Cameron, have insisted that generative AI is no substitute for human actors.

Lights, camera, action

Speaking to CBS ahead of the official release of 'Avatar: Fire and Ash', Cameron described his horror at encountering AI acting.

Quote of the day

This article is part of TechRadar Pro's QOTD project to provide an insight into the minds of the brightest and most recognized figures in the technology industry today and in years gone by. Read the full series here.

Having enjoyed a long and successful career in Hollywood, the filmmaker has dedicated the latter period of his career to the Avatar franchise.

This is primarily a means to explore innovation and the introduction of technology in cinema, with Avatar a torchbearer for 3D and its sequel extending it with new camera and performance-capture innovations.

One area that he's categorically unenthused about, however, is AI — and the use of generative AI as a substitute for human creative input, in particular.

Bad robot

After praising the motion-capture innovations in his film during the interview, he then opined on the "other end of the spectrum", expressing his disdain for the way that generative AI threatens to supplant creative input.

He described the notion of generating actors and performances simply using a text prompt as "horrifying" and said it's the opposite of what he was hoping to achieve with the technology being developed for the 'Avatar' film series.

Cameron is also the director of Stability AI, a company that delivers professional-grade generative AI tools for content creators. However, Cameron has insisted that generative AI can never create something completely original, based on the underlying transformer-based architecture that powers these systems.

Keumars Afifi-Sabet is a freelance contributor for Tech Radar and the Technology Editor for Live Science. He has written for a variety of publications including ITPro, The Week Digital and ComputerActive. He has worked as a technology journalist for more than five years, having previously held the role of features editor with ITPro. In his previous role, he oversaw the commissioning and publishing of long form in areas including AI, cyber security, cloud computing and digital transformation.

content_html_zh:
生成式人工智能的兴起无疑降低了电影创作的准入门槛，个人和大型制作公司都以不同的方式利用该技术。 但包括奥斯卡奖获奖电影制片人詹姆斯·卡梅隆在内的许多人坚持认为，生成式人工智能无法替代人类演员。

灯光、摄像机、动作

在《阿凡达：火与灰》正式上映前，卡梅隆在接受哥伦比亚广播公司采访时描述了他对人工智能表演的恐惧。

当日报价

本文是 TechRadar Pro 的 QOTD 项目的一部分，旨在深入了解当今和过去几年技术行业中最聪明、最受认可的人物的想法。 在这里阅读完整系列。

这位电影制作人在好莱坞享受了漫长而成功的职业生涯，并将其职业生涯的后期奉献给了《阿凡达》系列。

这主要是探索创新和引入电影技术的一种手段，《阿凡达》是 3D 的火炬手，其续集通过新的摄像机和表演捕捉创新扩展了它。

然而，他绝对不感兴趣的一个领域是人工智能，尤其是使用生成式人工智能来替代人类创造性输入。

坏机器人

在采访中赞扬了电影中的动作捕捉创新后，他对“光谱的另一端”发表了看法，表达了他对生成式人工智能威胁取代创意输入的蔑视。

他将仅使用文本提示来生成演员和表演的想法描述为“令人恐惧”，并表示这与他希望通过为“阿凡达”电影系列开发的技术实现的目标相反。

卡梅伦还是 Stability AI 的总监，该公司为内容创作者提供专业级的生成式人工智能工具。 然而，卡梅伦坚持认为，基于为这些系统提供动力的底层变压器架构，生成式人工智能永远无法创造出完全原创的东西。

Keumars Afifi-Sabet 是 Tech Radar 的自由撰稿人和 Live Science 的技术编辑。 他曾为多种出版物撰写文章，包括 ITPro、The Week Digital 和 ComputerActive。 他担任技术记者已有五年多，此前曾担任 ITPro 的专题编辑。 在之前的职位中，他负责监督人工智能、网络安全、云计算和数字化转型等领域的长篇文章的调试和发布。
